body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-29, on the merge commit for #1960 (`1b5417a2a`):

| run | created | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `Test Suite` [main] `33231406466` | 03:26:36Z | **pending, 0 jobs, 45+ minutes** |
| `Build & Push - Dev` [main], same commit | 03:26:36Z | completed / success |
| 15 runs on OTHER branches created after 03:26:36Z | later | all completed |

So it is not a FIFO queue: fifteen runs created after main's had already finished while main's had
not scheduled a single job. `gh run rerun` refused with "This workflow is already running".
Cancelling it and dispatching a fresh one with `workflow_dispatch --ref main` produced a second run
(`33232714755`) that ALSO sat pending with zero jobs, while branch runs kept dispatching normally
throughout.

Why it matters, and it is not cosmetic: main's post-merge Test Suite is the only thing that
verifies what actually landed. While it never ran, `Build & Push - Dev` for the same commit
completed and published — a live instance of F-7786b7 (":dev publishes from commits whose Test
Suite never passed"). Anything gating on "is main green?" reads `pending` forever, and a session
checking main's CI cannot distinguish "not yet run" from "never going to run".

Not diagnosed from outside: an account-level runner backlog and a main-specific scheduling fault
are indistinguishable through the API — both present as `status=pending, total_count=0`. What rules
a plain queue OUT is the 15-completed-after fact above.

Note `concurrency: group=${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`
means a wedged main run does NOT block the next one — a later main push supersedes it. So the
bounded harm is per-commit: that commit's verification is simply lost, silently.

Worth an explicit check somewhere: a run that has been `pending` with `total_count == 0` for more
than a few minutes should be reported as a CI fault, not read as "still running".

DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE ADDED 2026-08-29 ~04:10Z — this rules out the obvious alternative.
The natural reading of `pending, 0 jobs` is "the account is out of runners". It is not:

| run | ref | jobs |
|---|---|---|
| `33232714755` (workflow_dispatch) | main | **0**, 20+ min |
| `33231406466` (push) | main | **0**, 45+ min, then cancelled |
| `33232813185` (pull_request) | `fix/1961-cover-uuid-policy-guard` | dispatched within seconds; `ensure-mirror` 7s, `Classify image work` 20s, `validate-author` 18s, builds running |

A branch run scheduled real jobs in the same minutes that two main runs scheduled none. If the account had no runner capacity the branch run could not have started either, so the fault is specific to the `main` ref rather than to capacity. That is the test worth repeating if this recurs: dispatch on main AND push a throwaway branch, and compare — capacity failure hits both, a ref-scoped fault hits only one.

HYPOTHESES TESTED AND REJECTED (2026-08-29 ~04:15Z) — recorded so the next person does not
re-derive them:

1. **Runner/capacity exhaustion.** REJECTED. A `pull_request` run on a topic branch scheduled real
   jobs within seconds during the same minutes two main runs scheduled none.
2. **Concurrency-group deadlock** (`group: Test Suite-refs/heads/main`, `cancel-in-progress: true`).
   REJECTED by observation: the #1971 merge's push correctly cancelled the stuck predecessor
   (`33232714755` -> completed/cancelled), so the group was FREE — and the successor
   `33233012500` still sat pending with zero jobs.
3. **All jobs skipped by their `if:` conditions.** REJECTED by reading the workflow: `fast-tests`
   and `frontend-build` carry no job-level `if:` at all, so a push to main must schedule them.
   (And a fully-skipped run completes; it does not sit pending.)
4. **An expression that cannot evaluate on a push event.** REJECTED: both `inputs.*` references
   are guarded by `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&`, which short-circuits on push, so
   `inputs` is never dereferenced.
5. **A GitHub platform incident.** Not supported: githubstatus.com reported Actions and Webhooks
   `operational` throughout.

WHAT IS SPECIFIC, precisely: it is not the `main` ref and not the account. On main,
`Update Translations` completed/success and `Build & Push - Dev` reached in_progress from the SAME
push event that produced a Test Suite run with zero jobs. So the fault is the pair
(`Test Suite` workflow x `main` ref), and it survived three separate runs across two event types
(`push` twice, `workflow_dispatch` once).

NOT FIXABLE FROM A SESSION. `gh run rerun` refuses a pending run; cancelling and re-dispatching
reproduces the wedge. This needs someone with repository admin to look at Actions settings, or a
GitHub support ticket — or it self-resolves, in which case the useful artifact is this record of
what was already ruled out.

MITIGATION THAT HELD: PR-branch CI works, and `pr-lifecycle.sh` grades the head and refuses to
merge without a green gate, so #1960 and #1971 were both verified before landing. Main is
unverified BY CI, which is not the same as unverified — but anything that reads main's CI status
as a health signal is currently reading nothing at all, silently.

6. **A broken or unparseable workflow definition on main.** REJECTED. The only recent change to
   `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (532a35d80, #1842) adds `webkit` to a `npx playwright install`
   STEP inside `e2e-tests` — step-level, irrelevant to whether the run schedules. `yaml.safe_load`
   of main's copy parses cleanly: 6 jobs (`fast-tests`, `frontend-build`, `integration-tests`,
   `changed_paths`, `e2e-tests`, `test-summary`) and 3 triggers (`push`, `pull_request`,
   `workflow_dispatch`).

REPRODUCTION COUNT as of 04:20Z: **four** Test Suite runs on main with zero jobs, across two event
types — `33231406466` (push), `33232714755` (workflow_dispatch), `33233012500` (push),
`33233319897` (push). On each of those same pushes, `Update Translations` completed/success. The
pattern is stable and reproducible, not a transient.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE THAT MATTERS FOR ANYONE ACTING ON THIS: the tree itself is fine. `origin/main`
at `c0f3412dc` was verified directly in a detached worktree — **7460 passed, 106 skipped, 0
failed**, SHA identical before and after the run. So this is a REPORTING outage, not a broken
main. Do not revert anything on the strength of a red-looking CI page.
title: Test Suite runs on main sit pending with zero jobs while branch runs dispatch normally
